rows.title_full: AN ACT TO FURTHER AMEND SECTION THREE-A OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED NINE HUNDRED AND TEN, AS AMENDED, AND TO APPROPRIATE FUNDS TO IMPLEMENT ITS PROVISIONS(RE: RETIREMENT BENEFITS OF THE JUDGES OF THE LOWER COURTS)
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to extend to the judges of the lower courts the same retirement benefits accorded to the retired justices of the supreme Court, the Court of appeals and the Sandigan Bayan, by Republic Act No. 1797.  At present, the monthly pension which the retired lower court judges receive, remain pegged to the highest salary they were receiving at the time of their retirement, while the justices of the higher courts receive monthly pension equal to the monthly stipends of the incumbent justices.

rows.author: C011
rows.title_full: AN ACT REPEALING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8794 OR `AN ACT IMPOSING A MOTOR VEHICLE USERS' CHARGE ON OWNERS OF ALL TYPES OF MOTOR VEHICLES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES'
rows.abstract: Rationale: The RUT, at this time, is untimely. What it can only do is fuel protests and inflame passions, all for the P1 billion it can raise in a year.  Because RUT comes on the heels of the rise in oil prices and toll fees, and worsening traffic,it is akin to pouring gasoline on an already combustible mixture.  In short, it is a Trojan Horse, with the WB loan concelaed in its compartment. RUT is not a mere revenue-raising measure that will pester the present generation. It is a loan-releaseexpediter that will hound future Filipinos who will amortize the loan.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2000-07-18

rows.abstract: Rationale:  It will be noted that the government awarded 10,000 per square meters of land or one hectare to the farmers as assistance and credit line from the agri-agra law to finance the cultivation of land. If similar benefits can be extended to million market vendors, a healthy business climate will ensue and lead to economic recovery. The loand from private or government bank shows that the essence of equality in a democratic country is not lost in legality to the share of every Filipino toimprove the present stable marketing of the vendors.

rows.author: C091
rows.title_full: AN ACT BANNING THE ENTRY, SALE, PROCESSING, FIELD TESTING AND RELEASE OF PRODUCTS CONSISTING OF, CONTAINING OR DERIVED FROM GENETICALLY MODIFIED ORGANISMS (GMOS) INTO AND WITHIN THE COUNTRY AND IMPOSING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: "GMO Prohibition Act of 2000." The entry, sale, processing, field testing, release and similar acts, of products consisting of, containing or derived from genetically modified organisms (GMOs) into and within the country shall be banned in the Philippines for at least five (5) years after which the National Committee on Biosafety of the Philippines (NCBP), shall establish an efficient administrative procedure for granting permits and monitoring any direct, indirect, immediate or delayed effectsof GMOs on human health and the environment.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2000-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE NATIONAL TELECOMMUNICATI ONS COMMISSION (NTC) TO REGULATE, CONTROL AND MONITOR THE SALE OF SUBSCRIBER INFORMATION MODULE (SIM) PACKAGES OF CELLULAR PHONES AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES FOR ANY VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: The National Telecommunicati ons Commission (NTC) is hereby authorized to regulate control and monitor the sale of subscriber information module (SIM) packages of cellular phones in order to identify the true and real owners thereto. Every cellularphone dealer shall issue an invoice for each sale of SIM package. The invoice shall state the name and address of the purchaser or subscriber, the kind, standard and serial number of the particular SIM package purchased or subscribed.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2000-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING OIL COMPANIES TO INSTALL OIL SPILLAGE PREVENTIVE AND CONTROL MECHANISM IN THEIR TANKERS AND TO UNDERTAKE IMMEDIATE CLEANING OPERATIONS IN THE EVENT OF OIL SPILL WITHIN THE COUNTRY'S TERRITORIAL WATERS, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill seeks to require oil companies to install oil spill preventive and control facilities in their tankers and to undertake immediate and mandatory cleaning operations in the event of another oil spill within the country's territorial waters. Because of the oil spill whether caused by accident or otherwise, the use of beaches, harbors and marinas is seriously curtailed and temporarily halted until an effective clean up operation is compelted. The consequences of spilled oil from tankers plying the territorial waters of the Philippines vary from minimal damage to extensive deleterious effects on the marine ecosystem and the people living in the coastal areas.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2000-07-25

rows.author: A034
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE RECOVERY OF FINANCIALLY DISTRESSED ENTERPRISES AND THE RESOLUTION OF THEIR INDEBTEDNESS (RE:CORPORATE RECOVERY ACT)
rows.abstract: "Corporate Recovery Act." This bill represents  a comprehensive approach to the complex problems faced by enterprises when they, for whatever reason, can no longer pay their debts. It combines the creation of substative rights with relatively detailed procedural guidelines that move cases through court-supervise d proceedings quickly. It emphasizes the survival of the enterprise while at the same time keeping paramount the rights of creditors with duly registered liens against the enterprise'sassets.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2000-07-26

rows.title_full: AN ACT SEEKING TO IMPROVE CHILD PROTECTION AGAINST ABUSE, EXPLOITATION AND DISCRIMINATION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7610, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7658, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `SPECIAL PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AGAINST CHILD ABUSE, EXPLOITATION AND DISCRIMINATION ACT', APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks the more active involvement of government agencies like the Departments of Justice, Labor and Employment, Health and Tourism in child protection. Considering the government's thrust of decentralizatio n, this bill also provides for the greater participation of local social workers and law enforcers. CHILD PORNOGRAPHY is punshiable under this bill and mandates the creation of a central data bank to manitor the progress of child abuse cases.

rows.abstract: No person shall be appointed agriculturlist unless he is a citizen of the Philippines, a resident of the local government unit concerned, of good moral character, a holder of a college degree in agriculture or any related course from a recognized college or university, and a first grade civil service elgibile or its equivalent. He must have practiced his profession in agriculture or acquired experience in a related field for at least five (5) years in the case of the provincial or city agriculturist and three (3) years in the case of the municipal agriculturist.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2000-07-31

rows.author: C113
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXCLUDING BANK, NON-BANK FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES AND FINANCE COMPANIES FROM THE COVERAGE OF THE VALUE-ADDED TAX, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8424, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Countries which are now under the Value Added Tax (VAT) system have long recognized the difficulty of imposing the tax on banks and non-bank financial intermediaries primarily because of the limited VATable inputs that may be claimed as tax credits. Also, gross receipts of these institutions do not fir with the coverage of the regular VAT. It is the intention of this bill to ease out legislative work by totally exempting banks and non-bank financial intermediaries from the existing VAT system until such time that an appropriate tax structure is designed.
rows.status: Substituted by HB12237

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING FRANKING PRIVILEGE TO FILIPINO CITIZENS TO ENHANCE THEIR PARTICIPATION IN THE TASK OF GOVERNANCE
rows.abstract: "Franking Privilege Act of 2000." All Filipino citizens of legal age are hereby grnated franking privilege when addressing correspondence to any government agency or government-owne d or controlled corporations or their officials. the head of any such government agency or government-owne d or controlled corporation shall ensure that such correspondence shall be answered in writing within fifteen (15) days, stating therein any action taken for the information of its sender. If within 30 days, noanswer has been received, the sender may send a follow-up letter requesting for such an answer. If no answer is received within ninety (90) days from receipt of its follow-up letter, the responsible official shall be liable for vioaltion of Code ofConduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees if the sender decides to file a formal complaint against him.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2000-08-01

There shall be allowed an additional exemption of [Eight Thousand Pesos (P8,000.00)] SIXTEEN THOUSAND PESOS (P16,000.00) for each dependent not exceeding four(4).

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING TITLE II, ENTITLED `COASTWISE TRADE OF THE TARIFF & CUSTOMS CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES' ("PHILIPPINE EXPORT AND IMPORT FREIGHT SHIPPING ASSISTANCE ACT OF 2000"/CABOTAGE)
rows.abstract: "Philippine Export and Import Freight Shipping Assistance Act of 2000." This bill provides a stronger and clearer basis for foreign vessels to provide the transhipment services needed by our local exports and importers. Thus, a foreign vessel whichtransports foreign goods from a local port of transshipment to a local port of destination shall NOT be construed as engaging in coastwise trade.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE PUBLICATION, TELECAST, BROADCAST OR DISSEMINATION IN ANY MANNER OF THE RESULTS OF POLL SURVEY OF CANDIDATES WITHIN ONE (1) MONTH PRIOR TO AN ELECTION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Constitution envisions equal access to opportunities for public service. Elections are conducted so the people can rightfully choose the candidates who can best represent their interest in the proper forum.  Right choices are made when the people are provided witn ample time to be informed and to reflect on the qualifications of candidates for a given position. However, when poll survey results based on unverified data are released one month before election, this prerogative loses its meaning and the exercise of the right of suffrage greatly affected.

rows.abstract: Rationale: If thousands of people around the country who cannot afford to buy lots in expensive memorial parks die everyday, the existing public municipal cemeteries are certainly incapable of serving them.
